title: How Often Should You Send Marketing Emails?

facts.fact: The page recommends 1 to 3 campaign emails per week as the sweet spot for most ecommerce stores.
facts.quote: For most ecommerce stores, 1 to 3 campaign emails per week hits the sweet spot.

facts.fact: The page says the 1-3 weekly campaign range should keep unsubscribes under 0.3%.
facts.quote: low enough to keep unsubscribes under 0.3%.

facts.fact: Litmus reports that around 40% of ecommerce brands run on a weekly schedule by default (third-party claim cited by the page).
facts.quote: Litmus reports that around 40% of ecommerce brands run on a weekly schedule by default.

facts.fact: MarketingSherpa data shows 56% of unsubscribes happen specifically because content stopped being relevant (third-party claim cited by the page).
facts.quote: MarketingSherpa data shows 56% unsubscribe specifically because the content stopped being relevant.

facts.fact: The page's suggested cadence for high-frequency categories such as beauty, food, apparel, and pet supplies is 2-5 emails per week.
facts.quote: High-frequency safe (2-5 emails/week)

facts.fact: The page's suggested cadence for medium-frequency categories such as home and garden, toys, general retail, and health and wellness is 1-2 emails per week.
facts.quote: Medium-frequency (1-2 emails/week)

facts.fact: The page's suggested cadence for lower-frequency categories such as furniture, fine jewelry, and luxury goods is 2-4 emails per month.
facts.quote: Lower-frequency (2-4 emails/month)

facts.fact: For engaged subscribers (opened or clicked in the last 30 days), the page suggests 2-4 emails per week.
facts.quote: Send freely. 2-4 emails per week is fine, sometimes more during peak sale periods

facts.fact: For lapsing subscribers (no engagement in 30-90 days), the page suggests pulling back to 1 email per week.
facts.quote: Pull back to 1 email per week

facts.fact: For disengaged subscribers (no engagement in 90+ days), the page suggests a re-engagement sequence of 3-5 emails over 2-3 weeks.
facts.quote: Run a re-engagement sequence (3-5 emails over 2-3 weeks)

facts.fact: The page recommends a welcome email flow of 3-5 emails over 7-14 days for new subscribers.
facts.quote: 3-5 emails over 7-14 days for new subscribers.

facts.fact: The page recommends an abandoned cart flow of 3 emails over 24-72 hours.
facts.quote: Abandoned cart flow: 3 emails over 24-72 hours.

facts.fact: Abandoned cart flows recover an average of around 3% of lost sales, per Statista (third-party claim cited by the page).
facts.quote: Recovers an average of around 3% of lost sales per Statista

facts.fact: The page recommends a post-purchase flow of 4-6 emails over 30-60 days.
facts.quote: Post-purchase flow: 4-6 emails over 30-60 days

facts.fact: The page recommends a win-back flow of 3-5 emails for subscribers who have not bought in 60-120 days.
facts.quote: Win-back flow: 3-5 emails for subscribers who haven't bought in 60-120 days.

facts.fact: The page describes a spam complaint rate above 0.1% as a hard ceiling that can lead Gmail to filter email into the promotions tab.
facts.quote: Spam complaint rate above 0.1%. This is a hard ceiling.

facts.fact: The page flags an unsubscribe rate above 0.3% per send as a sign of sending too much.
facts.quote: Unsubscribe rate above 0.3% per send.

facts.fact: The page says that when two or more over-sending red flags occur at once, frequency should be cut by 25-30% for two weeks and re-measured.
facts.quote: cut frequency by 25-30% for two weeks and re-measure.

facts.fact: The page lists sending fewer than 4 emails per month (for a non-luxury brand) as a sign of sending too little.
facts.quote: You're under 4 emails per month, and you're not a luxury brand.

facts.fact: Per Omnisend research (third-party claim), promotional emails drive around 24% of total ecommerce sales.
facts.quote: promotional emails drive around 24% of total ecommerce sales
